Subject: Sudden 5xxs and latency spike starting 08:50 PDT

Hi Jasmine —

We started seeing a large increase in 504/502 responses and token latency ballooning across the eastus cluster starting around 08:50 PDT. Our app route (POST /v1/generate -> model: redwood-open-2-xl) started throwing intermittent 504s; p99 rose from ~180ms to >4.5s. This is hitting customer-facing workflows and our pager.

We captured a trace and a latency histogram (attached). From eyeballing the logs it looks like there were repeated prefetch attempts for a small set of very hot prefixes; there may be a caching loop or hot-key eviction thrash. Can you confirm? We need an ETA on mitigation — SLA exposure here.

Jordan

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Miller <jmiller@vivanta.com>
Date: 2029-10-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xxs and latency spike starting 08:50 PDT

Quick findings from initial diagnostics:
- Observed repeated prefetch churn on a handful of prefixes associated with Vivanta's high-throughput route. Prefetch requests rising 20x from baseline between 08:48–09:05.
- Hot-key occupancy on KV cache exceeded target occupancy; eviction pressure caused hot entries to be demoted, then immediately re-prefetched (thrash).
- There is a narrow batching window configured for this tenant (batch_timeout_ms=8) which is amplifying HOL blocking when the prefetch backlog grows; small windows + high prefetch concurrency => many small batches queued behind blocked hot keys.
- No downstream infra failures observed — root looks like cache misconfiguration combined with a sudden traffic fanout.

Attaching kv cache snapshot and quick grep of eviction markers. Proposed immediate containment: 1) apply temporary prefetch circuit: limit per-tenant prefetch concurrency to 4 threads and add 1s cooldown for hot prefixes; 2) increase batch_timeout_ms to 25ms for the Vivanta model route (reduces number of tiny batches and allows offloading synchronous prefetch); 3) pin top 20 hot prefixes in cache until rebalancing.

I'll standby to roll these changes with approval.

Attachments: kv_cache_snapshot.log
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Miller <jmiller@vivanta.com>
Date: 2029-10-25T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden 5xxs and latency spike starting 08:50 PDT

Looping in Marissa for exec visibility and to approve a short emergency change window. Summary for leadership: Vivanta (enterprise, committed Dedicated pool) is experiencing HOL blocking driven by prefetch churn on hot prefixes. Customer impact: elevated p99 and transient 5xxs; risk to SLA if not contained in the next 90 minutes.

Proposed emergency mitigations (runtime changes):
- Deploy prefetch circuit-breaker rule for Vivanta: max_prefetch_concurrency=4, hot_prefix_cooldown_s=1.
- Increase batch_timeout_ms from 8 -> 25 for the affected route.
- Temporarily pin top hotkeys (cache residency) for 30 minutes and run a controlled KV rebalance after traffic cools.

If leadership approves, we can apply the first two changes in the next 5–10 minutes (hot rollback available). After containment, follow-up: telemetry tuning (adaptive prefetch rates) and a postmortem with a runbook update.

— Ben
Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Approved: execute containment now. Decision rationale: containment buys us runway for a controlled rebalance without risking further SLA noise. Roll plan (ordered):
1) Apply prefetch circuit-breaker for Vivanta (max_prefetch_concurrency=4, hot_prefix_cooldown_s=1).
2) Bump batch_timeout_ms to 25ms for route (hot rollback to 8ms).
3) Pin top 20 hot prefixes via kv:pin API for 30 minutes.
4) Monitor p95/p99, prefetch queue depth, and eviction rate every 2 minutes; escalate to exec if p99 > 2s after step 2.

Post-containment: full KV rebalancing during an agreed 1-hour maintenance window and an after-action to update the prefetch backoff heuristics and runbook. Jordan: we'll confirm the exact maintenance time after containment.

Execution notes: Connor & Jasmine to run the change and report back in the thread when each step completes. Attach runbook excerpt for ops reference.

Attachments: runbook-prefetch-temporary-throttle.pdf
